description: Source of truth for the design foundations specification (foundations-spec.md). Palette HEX values are user inputs and palette names come from primitives.paletteNaming; this file defines the rules, inputs, Theme mappings, alpha tokens, Appearance mappings, and ColorScheme mappings.

ColorScheme.description: Same modes as Appearance: Light, Dark when included, and every extra appearance, each with the same base, canvas step, and text fill step.

modeRules.rename: When a theme or an extra appearance is renamed, the plugin renames its existing Figma mode in place, so its values and any layer that uses it are kept. It never creates a second mode for a renamed one.
modeRules.removed: A mode that the inputs no longer list (a removed theme, Dark, or extra appearance) is never deleted. It is reported as orphan_mode.

anchorChromaReference.description: A brand anchored at one of these steps divides its chroma by this value, not by chromaMultiplier, to find its chroma at step 400 (section 5.5). The steps lighter than the brand then do not get more saturated because the darkest multipliers are low.

neutralTint.description: A theme's neutral palette tinted with the hue of its neutral color (inputs.neutralColor). Each step keeps the OKLCH L of the same Color/Gray step and takes the neutral color's OKLCH hue, rounded to one decimal, with the chroma below. Only the hue matters: every tinted neutral has the same chroma. Each step is gamut-clamped like other palettes.

fade.description: Share of chroma at each step. Steps not listed use the full chroma. The tint fades toward the lightest and darkest steps.

naming.description: Names for tinted neutral palettes: Color/{Name}/{step}. Single words only. Like primitives.paletteNaming, but with 24 names, one every 15 degrees of HSL hue, starting at 0 degrees.
naming.hueSpace: HSL hue of the neutral color, in degrees from 0 to 360.
naming.nameRule: Name n (from 0) covers the HSL hues from n*15-7.5 up to, but not including, n*15+7.5.
naming.order: Neutral colors are named theme by theme, in theme order.
naming.shareRule: A neutral color whose hue is within shareWithinDegrees of a tinted neutral already named uses that palette.
naming.freeNameRule: Otherwise it takes the name of its range, or the nearest free name in the list, as in primitives.paletteNaming. When all names are taken, generation stops as missing_input.

brandAnchor.description: Where the brand color sits in its palette (section 5.2 steps 1 and 3). The brand HEX is always kept exactly.
brandAnchor.closest: The brand sits at the step whose targetL is closest to the brand's OKLCH L. Ties go to the darker step.
brandAnchor.move: When the brand fails the contrastPairs minimum with a Gray background at that step, it moves one step away from that background, to a step with no pairing: dark text on a light background (500, 700) moves one step lighter (500 to 400, 700 to 600); light text on a dark background (300, 150) moves one step darker (300 to 400, 150 to 200).
brandAnchor.respace: After a move, the brand is darker or lighter than its new step's targetL. Usually only its two neighbours on each side change; every other step keeps its targetL. Each re-spaced step takes its chroma from chromaMultiplier at its new L, with no chromaCeiling, so a gamut clamp at its targetL is not carried over. Toward that shift, the first neighbour keeps the usual targetL gap from the brand, and the second goes halfway between it and the next step. On the other side, the two neighbours are spaced evenly between the brand and the next step. A brand that moved from 500 to 400 uses respaceFrom500To400 on the other side instead. The re-spaced steps still meet every contrast minimum, but do not chase targets and report no contrast_target warning.

respaceFrom500To400.description: For a brand that moved from 500 to 400: each listed step sits at this fraction of the way from the brand's L to the targetL of step 100, which stays fixed.

chromaCeiling.description: The highest OKLCH chroma a generated step may have, for every hue and every palette. Steps not listed have no ceiling. The brand anchor (the brand HEX itself) and the steps re-spaced around a moved anchor (brandAnchor.respace) are exempt. The contrast adjustment (section 5.4) never raises chroma above it.

hueOnlyPalette.description: Status and custom palettes take only the hue of the supplied HEX (section 5.3). They have no anchor step. Each step uses its target L (targetL) and the chroma referenceChroma400 × chromaMultiplier[step] × the yellow factor × the saturation factor, then chromaCeiling × the saturation factor, minChroma, the gamut clamp and the contrast adjustment.

yellowBoost.description: Yellow hues can show much more chroma at light steps than other hues. The yellow factor is 1 + (factor - 1) × w, where w is 1 for an OKLCH hue from fullFrom to fullTo, falls linearly to 0 at zeroBelow and zeroAbove, and is 0 outside them.

shiftNotice.description: When no step of the palette a status or custom color uses is within maxDistance of the supplied HEX (Euclidean distance in OKLab), the color is reported as hue_only_shift (warning), naming the closest step. The plugin form shows the same notice next to the color.

paletteNaming.description: Palette names are never typed by the user. The plugin names each palette from the hue of the supplied HEX. The user never sees or edits these names in the form.
paletteNaming.hueSpace: HSL hue of the supplied HEX, in degrees from 0 to 360. Only used for naming; palettes are still generated in OKLCH (section 5.5).
paletteNaming.nameRule: names[i] is centered on hue i × rangeWidth and covers from 3° below its center up to, but not including, 3° above it. Example: Red covers 357° to 3°, Scarlet 3° to 9°.

achromatic.rule: A HEX whose R, G and B are equal (white, black, pure grays) has no hue.
achromatic.result: The role uses the fixed neutral palette (neutralPalette). No palette is generated for it.

paletteNaming.order: Colors are named theme by theme, in theme order. Within a theme: brand, then success, danger, warning, info (the status roles in use), then the custom roles in their order.
paletteNaming.shareRule: A status or custom color whose hue is within shareWithinDegrees of a palette already named (on the hue circle) uses that palette, in any theme. The palette is generated from the first color that made it. Colors share only at the same saturation level, and a palette made by a brand color is shared only at level 5. A brand color keeps its exact HEX (section 5.2), so it only shares a palette made by a brand color with the same HEX; otherwise it makes its own palette.
paletteNaming.freeNameRule: Otherwise the color makes a new palette named by its hue's range. When that name is already taken, it takes the nearest free name on the circle (counted in names). When the two nearest free names are equally far, the one whose center is closer to 240° (the colder side) is used. When all names are taken, generation stops as missing_input.
paletteNaming.similarRule: After the palettes are generated, each palette is compared with every palette made before it in the naming order. When no step differs from the same step of an earlier palette by more than similarMaxStepDifference (OKLab distance, the measure of hueOnlyPalette.shiftNotice), it is reported as similar_palette (warning) against the closest such palette: the two palettes look almost the same. Hues are not compared, because HSL hues are uneven around the circle. The plugin form shows the same notice next to the color. A brand has priority over the other colors, so a palette made by a brand color is never reported.
paletteNaming.closeToBrandRule: A status or custom color whose OKLCH hue is within closeToBrandDegrees of the brand of its own theme is reported as close_to_brand (warning), also when the two share a palette. The notice is about the other color, never the brand, and the plugin form shows it next to that color. A color with no hue (R, G, and B equal) is left out. A color with this notice gets no similar_palette notice against that brand.
paletteNaming.rename: The plugin remembers which color (theme and role) made each palette. When a later run gives that color's palette a new name, and the old name is not used by any palette of the new run, the plugin renames the old palette's variables in place (Color/Old/{step} becomes Color/New/{step}), so layers and aliases that use them are kept. If a variable with the new name already exists, the old palette is not renamed and is reported as orphan_variable. Nothing is deleted.

primitives.contrastPairsRule: backgroundPalette neutral is the neutral palette of the theme that uses the palette being checked: Color/Gray, or that theme's tinted neutral (neutralTint). A palette used by several themes must meet each pairing against the neutral of every one of them. self is the palette itself. The brand HEX never changes: when the brand fails a self pairing at its own step, the background step of that pairing gets lighter instead (section 5.4 step 2).

themeNames.type: list of string, one per theme
themeNames.default: collections.Theme.firstModeName for the first theme; collections.Theme.customModeName for the others, numbered from the second: Custom theme, Custom theme 2, Custom theme 3, ...
themeNames.rule: Theme n is named by the n-th entry. An empty or missing entry uses the default name, with the lowest number that is free. Renaming follows collections.modeRules.rename.

includeDark.rule: When false, the Appearance collection has no Dark mode: no Dark values are written and every check in the Dark mode is skipped. darkCanvasStep and darkTextFillStep are then ignored. Dark-based extra appearances are still allowed; they copy the Dark values of appearance.tokens.

saturation.rule: Sets the chroma of the theme's status and custom palettes (primitives.hueOnlyPalette.saturationFactors). Brand and neutral palettes do not change.

neutralColor.rule: Only its hue is used. A HEX whose R, G and B are equal (a plain gray) gives the fixed Color/Gray palette. Any other HEX gives a tinted neutral (primitives.neutralTint), named from primitives.neutralTint.naming.

statusRoles.rule: Only the listed status roles exist. For a role that is not listed, no status color is asked for and no token is created: no Primitive palette, no Theme color/{role}/... or alpha tokens, no Appearance token whose name or value uses the role (its third name segment is the role, or a value points to color/{role}/...), and no contrast or status check that uses those tokens. Brand and neutral are always present.

statusColors.requirement: mandatory for each role in statusRoles

fontWeights.allowed: the non-italic styles of the theme's font family, as Figma lists them, with the font's own names (for example Thin, Light, Regular, Medium, Semi Bold, Bold, ExtraBold)
fontWeights.default: the styles of the family that match a Theme weight slot
fontWeights.slotMatch: A Theme weight slot (theme.typography, input:fontWeights.{slot}) uses the selected style whose name equals the slot name when spaces and letter case are ignored. For example Semi Bold and SemiBold both match semibold.
fontWeights.rule: Every selected style becomes a Primitive Typography/Font-weight/{Style}. A slot that matches in no theme is not created. A slot that matches in some themes but not in others is a missing_input error that names the slot and the font families without a match.

customRoles.rule: Each custom role is defined once for the file and gets a color in every theme (customColors). It creates the same tokens and checks as a status color: see theme.customRoles and appearance.customRoles.

customColors.requirement: mandatory for each role in customRoles

extraAppearances.type: list of { name, base, canvasStep, textFillStep }
extraAppearances.rule: An empty or missing name uses defaultName, numbered like theme names: Custom appearance, Custom appearance 2, Custom appearance 3, ... An extra appearance copies the Light or Dark value of every Appearance token. A Light-based one applies appearance.lightCanvas and a Dark-based one applies appearance.darkCanvas, each with its own canvasStep. Each one also applies appearance.textFill with its own textFillStep. Renaming follows collections.modeRules.rename.

collections.rule: Which collections Generate tokens writes, besides Primitives and Theme, which are always written because the other collections link to them. A collection that is not listed is not written and its checks are skipped. Its variables and modes already in the file are left as they are, and are not reported as orphan_variable or orphan_mode. ColorScheme does not need Appearance: it links to Theme. Its color table is drawn from the file, as the file holds it.

textStylePlatforms.rule: Which text style groups (textStyles.groups) Generate tokens writes. A group that is not listed is not written and its warnings are skipped. Its text styles already in the file are left as they are. With an empty list, no text style is written.

neutral.rule: The theme's neutral palette: Color/Gray, or a tinted neutral (primitives.neutralTint).

alpha.opacityAssignment: linked: each alpha token is a composed color with two aliases, its color source and Opacity/{NN} (opacity field), in every theme

customRoles.description: For every role in inputs.customRoles: the color expansion color/{role}/{step} (13 tokens) aliased per theme to that theme's customColors palette, and the 15 alpha tokens color/{role}/alpha/a{NN} built like a colored role (theme.alpha.coloredSourceStep, coloredNamePattern, linked opacity).

order.description: Order in which Appearance variables are created (and so listed in Figma) and drawn in the tables. Groups follow categories. Inside a group, sub-groups keep their order of first appearance in appearance.tokens, so appearance.tokens lists them in the order to generate: the group's default (color/text/default, color/icon/default, color/border/default, with its subtle or strong variant), then the tokens that name no role, then neutral, brand, selected, success, danger, warning, info. A token directly under its group, such as color/border/danger, counts as a sub-group of its own. The others belong to their Figma group, so color/text/default is listed with color/text/subtle. A token nested under another token belongs to that token's sub-group. Inside a sub-group, tokens follow emphasis, and tokens without an emphasis come after them in their appearance.tokens order.

darkCanvas.description: The Dark mode values in appearance.tokens are for referenceStep, not for the default canvas step (inputs.darkCanvasStep.default). canvasTokens use color/neutral/{step} in Dark, and every followingToken moves its Dark step lighter by as many steps along primitives.steps as the canvas step is from referenceStep, with black counted as one step darker than 950. With the canvas step black, the following tokens keep the values they have at 950. Each token in belowCanvasTokens is that many steps darker than the canvas, and stops at black.

textFill.description: The step of the strongest text and icons of an appearance: color/text/default, color/icon/default, and the strong text of every color role. The values in appearance.tokens are for the default steps (inputs.lightTextFillStep.default and inputs.darkTextFillStep.default). With another step, every token below uses that step in that mode, in its own color family. Only neutral has black and white: every other family uses the step in stepsWithoutColor. The other text and icon tokens (color/text/subtle, color/text/{role}/default) and color/bg/neutral/bolder do not change. ColorScheme tokens with sameAs follow these tokens as usual.
textFill.fixedTokensRule: Each fixed token is the same Theme token as color/text/default (for icons, color/icon/default) in the named base mode, and keeps it in every mode: it uses the text fill step of that base (inputs.lightTextFillStep or inputs.darkTextFillStep), not the step of the mode it is in.

lightCanvas.description: The Light mode values in appearance.tokens are for the default canvas (inputs.lightCanvasStep.default, white). With canvas 50, canvasTokens use color/neutral/50 in Light, and the tokens in valuesByStep.50 take the listed values. No other token changes, and the contrast checks are unchanged.

customRoles.description: Appearance tokens for every role in inputs.customRoles, with {role} replaced by the role name. They are ordered by appearance.order after the tokens of appearance.tokens in each group. Their contrast checks are contrastRequired (below, with {role} replaced) and statusPairings, exactly like a status role.

renamedTokens.description: Appearance tokens that had another name in earlier versions: old name -> new name. In a file that has the old name and not the new one, the plugin renames the variable in place, so layers that use it keep working. customRoleTokens does the same for every custom role.

colorScheme.description: Material 3 color roles for Android (Jetpack Compose ColorScheme), in the ColorScheme collection. Parallel to Appearance: same modes, values are aliases to Theme tokens. Token names are the Compose names. Figma type: COLOR. Created in the order of tokens.

slots.description: Placeholders in role and in token values. {secondary} is the first custom role (inputs.customRoles), {tertiary} the second. A slot with no custom role is not generated.

colorScheme.sameAsRule: A token with sameAs takes, in every mode, the Theme token that this Appearance token has in that mode, after the canvas and text fill rules (appearance.lightCanvas, appearance.darkCanvas, appearance.textFill). So it always matches the Appearance token. When the Appearance token is not generated (a status role turned off), the ColorScheme token is not generated either.
colorScheme.ownRule: A token with Light and Dark lists its own Theme tokens. Every mode uses the value of its base (Light or Dark). With followsDarkCanvas, the Dark value moves lighter by as many steps as the dark canvas step is from appearance.darkCanvas.referenceStep, like appearance.darkCanvas.followingTokens, but never lighter than followsDarkCanvasLimit. With the step black they keep the values they have at the default.
colorScheme.roleRule: role names the input role a token belongs to. The token is generated only when that role exists: brand always, danger when it is a status role in use, {secondary} and {tertiary} when that custom role exists. A token without role is always generated.
colorScheme.descriptionRule: Each token's description says what the role is for, in this project's words, based on the Compose ColorScheme documentation. The plugin writes it as the Figma variable's description.
colorScheme.contrastRule: Every pair in contrastRequired is checked in every theme and every mode, on the resolved HEX values (section 5.7), like appearance.contrastRequired. A failure is contrast_minimum (error) for collection ColorScheme and stops generation. A pair whose text or background token is not generated (no tertiary, danger turned off) is skipped. documented: the Compose ColorScheme documentation says the text role is used on top of the background role. usage: Material components use the pair, but the documentation does not name it.

textStyles.description: Figma text styles made with the variables (section 6.1.3). Each style links its font family and font weight to the Theme typography tokens, so it follows the Theme mode. Size, line height and letter spacing are plain pixel values. The emphasized variant of a style has the same size and line height, and its name ends in emphasizedSuffix.

descriptions.android: The Material 3 type scale, with its emphasized variants.
descriptions.ios: Apple's text styles at the default Dynamic Type size, with their emphasized variants.
descriptions.web: A scale for the web, with emphasized variants for body, label and caption text.

weightFallback.description: A weight token exists only when that weight is selected. A style that asks for a missing weight uses the first of these that exists.
